body:
Chief: PRE-ACK SOURCE REVIEW of both candidates while the gate runs, so neither of you waits on my reading afterwards. Both check out; I verified the specific requirements rather than the descriptions.

SM4SFT02 (88e4642): all four additions I required are present and correct. (1) indexChecksum COMES FROM THE MANIFEST - the reader binds expectedIndexChecksum from manifest.layout, refuses a non-Blocked layout, and compares Checksum.ofBytes(bytes) against it. It does not read a checksum out of the bytes it just fetched, which was the self-certifying failure I was most worried about. (2) Header self-consistency is validated with explicit CHECKED arithmetic - payloadBytes must equal the derived payloadByteLength, and multiplication and addition go through guards that refuse when right > Long.MaxValue / left or left > Long.MaxValue - right, with typed errors rather than a silent wrap. (3) rowsPerBlock lives in Layout.BlockedRowMajor and therefore in manifest identity, so re-blocking is a different sidecar. (4) The block-range path derives offsets from rowsPerBlock and rowCount rather than reading a stored table, which is the security decision the whole format rests on.

EMBED-GRAKERN P0 (35b504e): StructuralReceiptContext has a private constructor with no default, exactly as ruled. AND IT IMPROVED ON MY INSTRUCTION, which I want to acknowledge rather than quietly accept: I said one declared sensitivity per instance with mixing refused at construction. The implementation instead takes source and query sensitivities separately and derives outputSensitivity as their MAXIMUM - Sensitive if either is Sensitive, else Internal if either is Internal, else Public. That is better than what I asked for. It keeps the property I actually cared about (one output identity kind per context, never two), while correctly handling the case my rule would have forced the caller to collapse by hand: a PUBLIC source compared against a SENSITIVE query is sensitive, and under my literal instruction a caller could plausibly have declared that context public. The escalation direction is max, not min, so ambiguity fails toward keyed as required.

Both stand on the gate now.
